title: Harness Engineering: Why Your Agent Got Better Without a Model Upgrade
excerpt: Vivek Trivedy's team moved a coding agent from Top 30 to Top 5 on Terminal Bench 2.0 by changing only the harness. OpenAI and Anthropic published harness essays six weeks apart. Here's what the discipline actually covers — and why observability, evaluation, and enforcement aren't adjacent to your agent, they're part of it.
author: Saurabh Kumbhar
seo_title: Harness Engineering Explained — Agent = Model + Harness (2026)
seo_description: Harness engineering, formalized by Vivek Trivedy and echoed by OpenAI and Anthropic, is the discipline behind agents that got better without a model upgrade. What a harness contains, why it goes stale, and why observability is a harness component.

title: Your Agent Has No Brakes: Notes on Loop Engineering
excerpt: Everyone designs the agent loop. Almost nobody designs what stops it. Field notes on inner-loop back-pressure versus outer-loop observation, the 'success is silent, failures are verbose' pattern, and why a multi-turn jailbreak like Crescendo is invisible to anything that sees one request at a time.
author: Saurabh Kumbhar
seo_title: Loop Engineering: Inner-Loop Back-Pressure vs Outer-Loop Observation
seo_description: Loop engineering is designing the agent's iteration cycle, not just the prompt. Inner loop blocks and raises; outer loop scores and accumulates. Why loops drift instead of crashing, and why trajectory-level detection beats per-turn classifiers.

title: EchoLeak: A Teardown of the Zero-Click Prompt Injection That Changed the Threat Model
excerpt: CVE-2025-32711 exfiltrated internal data from Microsoft 365 Copilot with no user interaction at all. A step-by-step teardown of the chain, the 2025 CVE wave around it, and the architectural conclusion: stop trying to build a model that can't be fooled, and build the system so that when it is, nothing important breaks.
author: Saurabh Kumbhar
seo_description: A full teardown of EchoLeak, the first documented zero-click indirect prompt injection against a production AI system — the kill chain, the 2025 CVE wave, MCP tool poisoning, cross-modal injection, and the containment surfaces that actually work.

title: Your Eval Number Is Measuring Your Pipeline: An Audit for LLM-as-Judge
excerpt: Position bias, verbosity bias, self-preference bias — all named, published, and reproducible. And a 2026 variance study attributes 40–60% of judge score variance to pipeline factors rather than the thing being evaluated. Five checks you can run on your own eval pipeline in an afternoon, plus why single-output scoring stopped being enough for agents.
author: Saurabh Kumbhar
seo_title: LLM-as-Judge Bias and Calibration — A Practical Eval Audit
seo_description: Position, verbosity, and self-preference bias are documented and reproducible, and 40–60% of judge score variance comes from pipeline factors. A five-check audit for your eval pipeline, plus trajectory-level agentic evaluation and eval drift.

title: We Published a Guardrail Benchmark We Don't Win
excerpt: Eight guardrails, four corpora, 949 cases. We came second on both output-side corpora and third on both input-side ones, and a 30-line regex control beats three of the eight contestants. Why benchmarketing is a forty-year-old problem, what makes a self-published benchmark worth reading, and the four methodology decisions that each cost us something.
author: Saurabh Kumbhar
seo_title: Benchmarketing: Why We Published a Guardrail Benchmark We Don't Win
seo_description: Every AI vendor benchmarks itself and wins. We ran eight guardrails over 949 cases and placed second twice and third twice, with a regex control, public corpora, and every miss listed by case ID. The credibility checklist and what it cost us to follow it.
